messages.subject: clarification on assocComp function output
parts:
Dear group,

 

I have read the documentation for the assocComp function and I have further questions or need clarification.

 

The values that come up as $pcs what do the values represent?  Are they a correlation coefficient of the methylation for all CGs against each of the principal components?

 

$vars I assume in the percentage that each of the principal components contributes to the variation in methylation

 

$associciation is the p-value for the association of each of the principal components against each of the variables tested.

 

If I am right, if PC1 contributes to 90% of the variation in methylation I SHOULD expect to get a significant p-value like 0.001 or more significant in the $association provided that I have identified and input one of the principal components?

 

 

 

Michelle

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] clarification on assocComp function output
parts:
The idea of this function is to find principal components associated with covariates such as age,sex and batches. If you find such components you can remove them from the data (removeComp() function), this is a way of dealing with covariates very crudely. 

If a principal component is significantly associated with a covariate you should get a low p-value regardless of what % of variation it explains.

Best,
Altuna
